rules.text: International students must register at the local Public Security Bureau (PSB) within 24 hours of checking into private accommodation, or within 30 days for those living in university dormitories.

International students may open a personal RMB bank account at major Chinese banks (ICBC, Bank of China, CMB, etc.) by presenting a valid passport, valid visa or residence permit, PSB registration certificate, and enrollment certificate.
The minimum initial deposit for an ICBC UnionPay debit card (student card) is CNY 20.
Bank of China requires a permanent address proof (dorm contract or rental agreement) in addition to the standard documents for international students.

Inbound personal remittances to China exceeding the equivalent of USD 50,000 per calendar year must be reported to SAFE (State Administration of Foreign Exchange) by the receiving bank. The individual may be required to provide source-of-funds documentation.

CNAPS (China National Advanced Payment System) is the mandatory interbank payment infrastructure for all CNY transfers within China. Tuition payments must use the university's official CNAPS account number.
Chinese universities are prohibited from accepting tuition payments through unauthorized third-party agents. Payments must be made directly to the university's official bank account using CNAPS.

The People's Bank of China (PBOC) sets the daily CNY/USD central parity rate. All commercial banks quote retail rates within a +/-2% band around the central parity. INR/CNY rates are derived via the USD cross-rate.
International students may open a bank savings account at Chinese commercial banks; this constitutes the first step in establishing a financial relationship in China.
A UnionPay debit card issued to an international student by a Chinese bank enables domestic card transactions and is the prerequisite for applying for a credit card.
Alipay and WeChat Pay accounts linked to a Chinese bank account allow digital payment history to be accumulated.
ICBC offers a secured credit card to some international customers; eligibility, minimum deposit, and credit limit vary and must be confirmed with the branch. No guarantee of approval is implied.
Credit card usage and repayment history is reported to the PBOC Credit Reference Center monthly by credit-issuing banks. Consistently paying in full and on time builds a positive record.
Individuals may request their own PBOC credit reference report once every 30 days, free of charge, via the PBOC's online portal or at a PBOC branch.

International students must obtain a student visa (X1 for programs longer than 6 months, X2 for programs 6 months or shorter) before entering China. An X1 visa must be converted to a Residence Permit within 30 days of arrival at the local PSB Exit-Entry Administration.

The Chinese Ministry of Education warns that unauthorized agents charging fees or discounts for university admissions or tuition payments are fraudulent. All fees should be paid directly to the institution.
